title: Kurz und klar: Redemittel und Grammatik

blocks.title: Was du kannst

paragraphs.text: This page collects everything the chapter gave you, in two halves. The top block is the language you can now say — the questions and answers you need to open a conversation and to keep it going. The bottom block is the machinery underneath it, printed as tables so you can check yourself without rereading ten pages.
Was machen Sie gern? · Gehen wir ins Kino? · Was sind Sie von Beruf? · Wann haben Sie frei?
Four questions carry the whole chapter: what you like, when you meet, what you do, when you are free. If you can ask them, the first ten minutes of any conversation are yours.
Ja, sehr gern. · Nein, nicht so gern. · Es geht so. · Nein, das geht leider nicht.

Four answers that shade from enthusiasm to refusal, and they belong together — learn them as a set and you are never stuck for a reply. The same shape works for work: ask with {{de:sein}}, answer with a job, ask with {{de:haben}} and name the free day.
Was sind Sie von Beruf? — Ich bin Studentin. Wann haben Sie frei? — Am Montag.
der Arzt → die Ärzte · das Buch → die Bücher · die Stunde → die Stunden · das Auto → die Autos

The verb table, the yes/no question, the three articles and the plural endings are all collected below, exactly as the textbook prints them. Read them once more, then go back to whichever exercise still feels slow.
ich koche · du kochst · er/sie/es kocht · wir kochen · ihr kocht · sie/Sie kochen
ich bin · du bist · er/sie/es ist · wir sind · ihr seid · sie/Sie sind

bullets: You can ask what somebody likes to do and answer in three shades — keen, not really, so-so.
You can arrange a meeting and turn one down without sounding rude.
You can name all seven weekdays and put the right one after am.
You can say what you do and what somebody else does, with the right ending on the verb.
You can ask and answer two questions about work: what you do for a living, and when you are free.
You can count from 21 into the thousands and read a figure like 74.300 aloud.
You can put a noun under der, das or die and build its plural.
You can fill in a German registration form with your own details.
